newsitem.title: UK: BZW to build links in key areas.
newsitem.headline: BZW to build links in key areas.

text.p: BZW, the investment banking arm of Barclays Plc, plans to improve links between its key areas to build profitable business, its chief executive Bill Harrison said on Tuesday.
Harrison said there are three key areas which could be developed.

These are acquisition finance which could be linked more closely to activities in corporate finance and advice, equities -- where the bank's secondary market presence and distribution capabilities are to be used to get more primary or origination business -- and markets which Harrison said is strongly placed to make significant earnings.
"It's perfectly evident that the Markets area needed a significant upgrade," Harrison said. "That business is re-tooled now and is strongly placed to make a significant earnings contribution."
Harrison said one of the areas BZW is looking to develop is Japan with special emphasis on the Japanese government bond (JGB)market.
Harrison said he intends to "take the business as it stands and squeeze out more productivity."
BZW announced a 29 percent fall in pre-tax profits for 1996 at 204 million stg characterised by underperformance in some areas and a high level of spending on new staff and systems.
